description: Cascaded multi-stage TEC. Each stage pumps heat from its cold side to its hot side; the hot side of stage k = cold side of stage k+1. Inter-stage temperatures found by equating heat flows. Overall COP = Q_c_stage1 / W_total. COP per stage < single-stage at same total dT.

unit.name: Generic 2-stage cascaded Bi2Te3 TEC — stage-1 (cold) + stage-2 (hot)
unit.source: Goldsmid, H.J. (2010). Introduction to Thermoelectricity, Springer; Rowe, D.M. (Ed.) (2006). CRC Handbook of Thermoelectrics; Riffat & Ma (2003). Appl. Thermal Eng. 23, 913-935; Chein, R., Chen, Y. (2005). Int. J. Refrig. 28, 828-839.

n_stages.note: Number of cascade stages (1=single-stage, 2=two-stage; extend as needed)

stage_1.note: Cold (bottom) stage — largest temperature span, highest ZT utilization

stage_2.note: Hot (top) stage — narrower span, smaller modules or lower current

n_modules.note: Stage-2 needs more modules since it must pump Q_c + W_stage1

COP_degradation_per_stage.note: Fraction of ideal COP retained per additional stage due to thermal contact resistance and junction losses; from Chein & Chen (2005) two-stage experimental data

contact_resistance_K_per_W.note: Thermal contact resistance at inter-stage interface (spreader + TIM); Riffat & Ma (2003)
